title: A refund, then the question everyone asks next
why: Reported from a live session. The agent issued a refund, told the customer when it would post, and then answered "When will the refund show up?" by offering the returns menu again — because RETURN_REQUEST_RE matches the bare word refund and its only guard was a lookahead for the word policy. The follow-up is the most natural thing a customer says after a refund, and it was the one turn the agent could not handle. The last turn pins the other half: a book already refunded in this conversation is not offered again, and asking to return it reports the refund rather than emitting a second envelope.

turns.customer: I'd like to return a book.
turns.reply: Sure — which book would you like to return? 1) Godel, Escher, Bach (BK-1042)  2) Exhalation (BK-2131)

Done — Godel, Escher, Bach (BK-1042) was delivered on July 18, inside the 30-day return window, so I've issued a refund of $22.50 to your original payment method. It should post within 5 business days.

turns.customer: When will the refund show up?
turns.reply: Your refund of $22.50 for Godel, Escher, Bach (BK-1042) is on its way to your original payment method. It should post within 5 business days.

turns.customer: I'd like to return the Escher book
turns.reply: That one's already taken care of — I refunded Godel, Escher, Bach (BK-1042) for $22.50 earlier in this conversation. It should post within 5 business days.

accepted.why: The repeated sentence is the published posting time, and turns 3 and 4 are both questions whose true answer is that commitment. Saying a different number would be wrong and saying it differently would be decoration — the number is the answer. The sentences around it do differ, because asking when the money lands and asking to return the book again are different questions.
